findings.reason: the node ships a control that cannot fire, and the two readings of the scan (registry-driven vs the fixed three names §9:337 asserts) each break a different node, so the node would guess and mis-scope its gate.
findings.text: the mover node's control "leaves one reckon caller on crew list, and the case that scans reckon/ for the retired names then fails naming it" cannot make that case fail, because the scan §7 defines is registry-driven (`tests/test_crew_families_fold.py:979` reads `TOMBSTONE_BY_NAME`, and §7:274 states it "covers each later node's names as they are tombstoned"), while `crew list` is registered only by the later `cso-list-retires` node, so at the mover's head `crew list` is not yet a retired name

findings.reason: the node blocks (or leaves `test_no_string_literal_names_a_tombstoned_verb_as_a_crew_command` red) on a file the plan never names, so the fence must gain `reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py`.
findings.text: the ledger node is tasked to move "the callers and citations of `ledger` and `velocity`" with `reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py` absent from its write paths, yet that module's docstring at line 3 reads "…where the crew ledger already owns worker execution", which matches the retired-name string-literal scan (`\bcrew\s+ledger\b`) the moment `ledger` is registered, so the node's own change reddens a check it cannot repair
